subject: goldfish aquarium
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Fish Tank?

scenes.text: What if you never cleaned your fish tank? The water could look clear while it poisons the fish.
Fish breathe out ammonia through their gills. Above a tiny 0.05 milligrams per litre, it starts damaging their tissue.
Bacteria in the filter turn it into nitrite, then nitrate. That team takes six to eight weeks to grow.
Skip water changes for months and nitrate piles up. Algae explodes, and the water slowly turns acidic.
Then the trap: a sudden huge clean swings the chemistry back, and fish can die right after.
Yet a sealed glass ball with shrimp and algae can run for years without cleaning. Balance beats scrubbing.

description:
What if you never cleaned your fish tank? Fish release ammonia through their gills, and University of Florida experts say tissue damage can start above 0.05 mg/L of un-ionised ammonia.
Filter bacteria take six to eight weeks to establish, nitrate builds up between water changes, and a neglected tank can turn acidic, so one sudden big clean can shock the fish.
